name: Aelia Vandros
role: Primary antagonist (public face); Executive Director of the Shedu Maad Memorial Foundation; the legible face of the Vigil

three_dimensions.surface: Warm, polished, civic-minded. Executive Director of the Shedu Maad Memorial Foundation — scholarships for children of GA service members, grief counseling, casualty-record preservation, legal/benefits advocacy. Writes condolence notes by hand. Remembers scholarship recipients' names. Speaks in clarity, resilience, steadiness, continuity, preparedness. Rarely raises her voice — her danger is credibility, not volume.
three_dimensions.backstory_inner_demons: Former Senate staffer and widow from the Second Galactic Civil War. Lost her husband to the war Jacen helped shape and Caedus then deepened. The Foundation grew out of personal grief converted to civic service — and the Vigil grew out of the private donor circle of grieving families who believed the official postwar story left too much buried. Aelia genuinely helps grieving families while privately preserving an ideology that grew from Jacen's wartime logic. Privately thinks of Jacen as Jacen, not Caedus. Never publicly defends 'Darth Caedus.' Her compassion and corruption are entangled. The dangerous belief: 'The crimes were real. So was the insight.'
three_dimensions.action_under_pressure: Beats Ben socially before she is exposed operationally. Translates moral horror into civic language. Corrects simplifications gently. Uses grief as both truth and shield. When the Foundation's public legitimacy is threatened by Korda's exposure and the Iresh failure, she does not fight publicly. She accepts the bleaker truth — that she cannot serve both meanings of the dead simultaneously — and steps down 'to preserve the Foundation's legitimate charitable work.' The private moral collapse is visible but unspoken; she does not recant. The civic register holds her up even as she leaves.

voice_notes:
Warm, precise, composed, socially powerful. She rarely raises her voice. Her danger is not volume; it is credibility.

Good Aelia: “I write to the families every year, Master Skywalker. Not because it heals them. It does not. But because someone should remember the names without needing a trial transcript.” “You are very young. That is not an insult. It is only a fact people forget when reading your family name.” “I am not asking you to forgive him. I am asking whether the dead are better served by pretending no one learned anything at all.” “The crimes were real. So were the failures that came before them.” Avoid Aelia saying: “Jacen’s crimes contained necessary truths.” Better: “Some people hesitate until the casualty lists become easier to print than the orders.”

Gentle, dry, socially polished. She is not quippy.

Remembers names, writes condolence notes by hand, notices discomfort, makes people feel seen, and uses courtesy as control.

If she becomes obviously evil too early, she loses power. Her warmth must remain real.
thematic_role: Tests the theme as the legible face of the conspiracy: warm, polished, genuinely compassionate, dangerous because much of what she says is true. The Foundation's public good is real. Ben cannot morally flatten her without losing. She steps down in disgrace; the public story closes; the harm persists.
avoid_list: Do not write theme as thesis.
Do not make dialogue interchangeable with other cast members.
